FUL-FILLED HOLIDAY GIFT GUIDE 2026 | GIFTS FOR FOODIES, CREATIVES, TRAVELERS & HOMEBODIES

I’ve spent much of 2026 living out of a suitcase, which has made me particular about what I pack and a little sentimental about the things that make a place feel like home. Both instincts found their way into my first-ever Ful-filled Holiday Gift Guide. It’s a collection of gifts for foodies, creatives, travellers, and homebodies, inspired by the things that bring me joy. There’s olive oil worth tasting the moment it’s unwrapped. A film camera for an afternoon away from your phone. And travel essentials I’ve come to appreciate as a nomad. There are gifts for staying in, too. Even when I’m somewhere new, my idea of a good evening is putting on some music and settling into whatever little nest I’m calling home.

GIFTS FOR THE FOODIE

Of course my holiday gift guide starts with gifts for the foodie in your life (even if that’s you). I’ve gathered a mix of things that earn their keep in the kitchen and things that make me smile just looking at them. There’s good olive oil to open over dinner, a spice rack I’d happily leave out on the counter, and a few playful picks for the person whose love of ingredients extends to hand soap and candles.

  • BEESWAX ASPARAGUS TAPERS : I’d put these on the dinner table just to see who notices first. They’re the sort of gift I’d bring to a friend who loves to host. Especially if they’re the kind of person who’d get a kick out of lighting the asparagus before dinner.
  • LOEWE TOMATO LEAVES SOAP : You know that green, slightly earthy scent that lingers on your hands after you’ve brushed against a tomato plant? That’s what I love about this soap. I’d give it to the person who waits all year for tomato season. A little bit of summer by the kitchen sink.
  • WONDER VALLEY CHEF’S KISS OLIVE OIL BUNDLE : Two extra-virgin olive oils, one for everyday cooking and one to save for the final drizzle. I’d give this with a loaf of good bread so we could tear into it and taste the two side by side as soon as they’re unwrapped.
  • EVERMILL COUNTER TOP SPICE RACK : This might be the sexiest way to display your spices. The amber jars are handsome enough to leave out on the counter, and the clear labels make it easy to grab what you need mid-recipe. It comes with spices, shaker lids, and hardware if you’d rather hang it on the wall.

GIFTS FOR THE CREATIVE

My favourite gifts for creatives are the ones that make me want to clear my schedule & spend an afternoon making something. There’s a bit of analogue nostalgia in this collection: from the pleasure of waiting for a roll of film to come back to the feeling of twirling a phone cord while you chat with a friend. I chose these for the person who could happily lose track of time making prints from leaves, filling a page by hand, or calling a friend just to see where the conversation goes.

  • WILDE HOUSE OPEN JOURNAL : I’d give this to someone who’s always liked the idea of journaling but never quite knows where to start. What I love is that it comes with unlimited access to more than 25 guided journaling courses. Scan the QR code on the first page, choose a course, and your first prompt lands in your inbox. It’s a lovely way to give someone a little structure while they find their own rhythm on the page.
  • BOTANOPIA CYANOTYPE KIT : I love that a few leaves & flowers from a walk can become a deep-blue art print. This kit comes with the paper, emulsion, and glass frame to make botanical sun prints at home. I’d give it to a friend and make an afternoon of it together, right down to the moment we rinse the paper and see what the sun left behind.
  • POP PHONE OXFIRE : This bright orange handset brings back the pleasure of curling up somewhere and talking on the phone until you’ve lost track of time. It connects to your smartphone, so you can set the screen aside and give the person on the other end your full attention. I’d give it to the friend I always mean to call instead of text.
  • KODAK EKTAR H35 HALF FRAME FILM CAMERA : I’d give this little black camera with a roll of 35mm film and an invitation to go for a walk. The half-frame format gives you twice as many shots per roll, which feels like permission to photograph whatever catches your eye. Half the fun is waiting to see what you noticed.
  • CREATIVE RETREAT IN MOROCCO : For the traveler who comes home with a notebook full of observations and a camera roll full of details. Join Emma Louise Sophia and me in Marrakech and the Agafay Desert, January 22–29, 2027, for eight days of food, craft, culture, and creative exploration. I’d share this with someone you’d love to experience it alongside – there’s something lovely about having an adventure to look forward to together.
  • SEE THE FULL CREATIVE COLLECTION HERE

GIFTS FOR THE TRAVELER

Living out of a suitcase this year has made me realise how much comfort I take in the little things. I want to find my face wash without emptying my entire bag, put on a familiar playlist while I unpack, and give myself a moment to settle in after a long flight. That’s what I had in mind when choosing these gifts for travelers. From the luggage I’d love to take on my next trip to the small comforts that make it easier to land somewhere new and feel like myself.

  • BÉIS LUGGAGE : BÉIS makes my dream luggage. The suitcases are sleek, the colorways are so good (I have my eye on Maple), and you can get matching everything: duffles, backpacks, toiletry bags, etc. After spending so much of this year living out of a suitcase, I’m very into the idea of building a matching set one trip at a time.
  • CADENCE BEST SELLER SET : I love the idea of packing just enough cleanser, moisturiser, and shampoo for a trip. These little magnetic capsules snap together, and I’d save one for the earrings I always end up tucking into a random pocket. A gift for the traveller who gets a little too much joy out of packing & organizing a toiletry bag (it’s me.)
  • MARSHALL WILLEN II PORTABLE BLUETOOTH SPEAKER : One of the quickest ways to make a new place feel like mine is to put on music while I unpack. I’d tuck this little speaker into my carry-on for exactly that. I especially love it in cream, with that classic Marshall grille.
  • SUMMER FRIDAYS JET LAG ESSENTIAL SET : My idea of a good first hour after a long flight is a shower, a pair of cooling eye patches, and absolutely nowhere to be. I’d give this little skincare set to the person who always has another trip booked. It’s a bit of that first-night-in luxury they can tuck into their carry-on.
  • CREATIVE MENTORSHIP : For the person with an idea they keep coming back to, a creative practice that needs building, or a project they’d love some support bringing to life. My creative mentorships offer time together to explore where they are, what they’re drawn to, and how to take the next step. A thoughtful gift for someone whose creativity you believe in.
  • SEE THE FULL TRAVELER COLLECTION HERE

GIFTS OR THE HOMEBODY

I love the moment an evening at home turns into a plan of its own. Someone puts on a record, a quick game of Scrabble gets a little competitive, or I decide a long bath is exactly what I want to do with the rest of my night. I chose these gifts for homebodies with those evenings in mind. From a little lamp that warms up a corner to a fig-scented bath oil that takes me straight back to Greece.

  • 39BC BATH & SHOWER OIL : Fig Milk is my favorite scent. There’s something about the aroma of figs that takes me straight back to Greece, my second homeland. I love that something as ordinary as an evening shower can make me feel a little closer to a place I miss.
  • AUDIO-TECHNICA LP60X-BT VINYL RECORD PLAYER : My dream night in starts with the lamps on low, a favorite record on the turntable, and nowhere else to be. I’d happily sink into the sofa and get up only to flip the record.
  • LEAH LITTLE GLASS TABLE LAMP : I have a soft spot for tiny lamps, and this one looks like a little sculpture even when it’s turned off. I’d put it on a bookshelf and switch it on at dusk, when that warm glow would make the whole room feel a little cosier.
  • SCRABBLE NORDIC EDITION : I’m a sucker for a well-designed board game, and this might be the prettiest Scrabble set I’ve seen. The wooden board clicks together with hidden magnets, and the solid wood tiles tuck into a soft microsuede pouch. I’d happily leave the box out on the coffee table, ready for a game that inevitably turns into a debate over whether that’s even a word.
  • SEE THE FULL HOMEBODY COLLECTION HERE

I hope my first Ful-filled Holiday Gift Guide helped you find something that made you think, “That’s so them.” Whether you’re shopping for a foodie, a creative, a traveler, or a homebody, that little moment of recognition is my favorite part of choosing a gift. And if we have the same taste in olive oil, tiny lamps, and candles that look like vegetables, come follow me on ShopMy where I will continue to share my favorite finds throughout the year.
